This BMW X5 M Was Over $120K New, Just Sold for Less Than Half After 43,500 Miles
15 photos
Photo: Cars&Bids
Depreciation tends to hit some cars like a freight train. Take this 2022 model year BMW X5 M Competition , for instance, which just sold for less than half the money it cost its first owner a few years ago.
As mentioned above, it is a 2022 model year machine, which was $120,695 new, according to the attached window sticker. How much do you think it went for? Normally, we would have kept this information close to our chest until the end of the story, but we’ll make an exception this time. The number was $55,000.
The crossover was advertised at the excitement of no reserve at an online auction on Cars&Bids that ended on October 26, 2026, and it found a new home for itself quite easily, proving that you don’t have to break the bank in order to own a modern performance-oriented machine. In fact, it cost less than a new Toyota Land Cruiser , which requires spending a minimum of $58,180, before destination, options, and dealer fees.
And if you think that the mileage is in the six-digit territory, then you clearly haven’t paid attention to the title, because this 2022 BMW X5 M Competition had a decent 43,500 miles (70,000 km) on the clock at the time of cataloging. It has a clean North Carolina title, and is still located in Charlotte, though not for long, because it will soon be on its way to its new owner.
Photo: Cars&Bids The vehicle has a Black Sapphire Metallic exterior paint finish beneath the matte blue vinyl wrap, which is said to have been applied some two years ago, and should be removed within five to seven years, according to the seller. Other modifications include the leather and Alcantara-wrapped steering wheel, the paddle shifters with capacitive touch bypass, and a RaceChip GTS Black tuning module.
As a result, this BMW X5 M could produce a bit more power compared to the standard one. However, we do not know the numbers, because a dyno chart was not supplied. With zero outside intervention, the twin-turbocharged 4.4-liter V8 engine develops 617 hp (460 kW/625 ps) and 553 lb-ft (750 Nm) of torque, with the peak torque available at 1,800-5,800 rpm, and the maximum output at 6,000 rpm.
The twin-turbocharged V8 engine rockets this model from 0 to 62 mph (0 to 100 kph) in just 3.9 seconds, and up to an electronically limited top speed of 155 mph (250 kph). With the optional M Driver’s Pack, the maximum speed increases to 180 mph (290 kph). An eight-speed automatic transmission delivers everything to the xDrive all-wheel drive system
Stuff such as the M Competition Package, Executive Package, Competition Package 2, and Drivers Assistance Pro Package are mentioned in the ad, alongside the heated front and rear seats, ventilated and massaging front seats, and 21-inch wheels at the front, and 22-inch wheels at the rear.
But what about the known flaws, you ask? Well, these include some chips in the windshield and on the hood, scratches on the wheels , scuffs on the driver’s door card, creases on the driver’s seat, and some scratches and pinholes in the vinyl wrap. Moreover, this BMW X5 M is said to have sustained “minor” damage to its right side two years ago, in October 2024.
Photo: Cars&Bids The service history reveals that the engine oil and filter were changed in January 2026, at 35,736 miles (57,512 km), and that the sunroof seal, dashboard, front passenger seat bottom leather, and front windshield washer pump strainer were replaced in June 2025, at 31,440 miles (50,598 km). The four tires were replaced, mounted, and balanced in January 2025, at 27,162 miles (43,713 km), and that is also when the rear brake pads were replaced, and the engine oil and filter were changed.
Additional service entries are also mentioned in the ad, which shows that the BMW X5 M in question is accompanied by the factory steering wheel, the OEM paddle shifters and touch sensor module, a flat tire kit, the owner’s manual, and two keys. The seller claims to have bought the super crossover from a dealer in January 2025, adding some 16,400 miles (26,400 km) since.
Now, we already told you how much this 2022 BMW X5 M Competition went for, but how much is one of these in today’s used car market in the States? Depending on the usual factors, that would be between $50,000 and roughly $75,000. High-mileage examples can dip below $50K, and low-mileage ones, with less than 30,000 miles (48,000 km) on their odometers, featuring plenty of gear, can pull close to the $70,000 mark.
Therefore, in theory, this BMW X5 M should have gone for more than $55,000, which was the selling price, but how much would it have been worth in your opinion? The listing can be accessed here on the quoted website.
